questions.q: How does the storefront app run right now, before this lesson's work?
options: Inside a Docker container on AKS
Started directly on the Azure VM's OS by a systemd service
On an AWS EC2 instance
It doesn't run anywhere yet
questions.explain: The app currently runs the way the Beginner project left it: installed directly on the VM and started by a systemd service.

questions.q: Why must containerizing the app happen before Lesson 4's Terraform and Lesson 5's pipeline?
options: Docker is required by AWS
Both the AKS cluster and the pipeline's deploy step need an image to actually deploy
Terraform cannot run until Docker is installed on the laptop
It doesn't need to happen first; order doesn't matter
questions.explain: Everything downstream — the cluster Terraform provisions and the pipeline's deploy step — assumes there's already a container image to run.

questions.q: In the two-stage Dockerfile, what does the `runtime` stage actually contain?
options: The full Go compiler toolchain
The app's production dependencies (installed fresh) plus only the compiled `dist/` folder copied from `build`
An exact copy of every layer from the `build` stage
Nothing but an empty base image
questions.explain: `runtime` runs its own `npm ci --omit=dev` and copies in only `dist/` from `build` — none of `build`'s other layers carry over.

questions.q: Why does `runtime` run its own `npm ci --omit=dev` instead of copying `node_modules` from `build`?
options: Because `npm ci` is faster than `COPY`
Because mixing dev and production installs between stages is a common source of subtly broken runtime images
Because Docker doesn't allow copying `node_modules` between stages
Because `build` never installs `node_modules` in the first place
questions.explain: Each stage resolves its own dependency tree for the environment it represents, rather than carrying a mismatched install forward.

questions.q: What is the minimum bar for success in this lesson, before Terraform or the pipeline exist?
options: The image deploys successfully to AKS
The CI/CD pipeline runs without errors
The containerized app responds correctly when tested locally, e.g. a clean 200 OK from a health endpoint
The AWS backup bucket is created
questions.explain: This lesson's goal is proving the container runs the app correctly on its own, before any infrastructure or pipeline work begins.
